The Fractal North currently ranks as the top pick in our roundup of the best PC cases, and it’s down to its lowest price all year for Black Friday at Amazon. It’s 25% off, bringing the $154.99 list price down to $115.99. That’s just slightly off the case’s all-time low on Amazon at $109.97, which it hasn’t dropped to in over a year.

Fractal Design's modern, classic, trendsetting PC case design is currently on sale. This mid-tower has enthusiast-friendly features and excels due to its looks, thoughtful design, and airflow.

There are a handful of variations of the Fractal North, three of which are available at $115.99: Charcoal Black/Dark Walnut with tempered glass, Charcoal Black/Walnut with mesh, or White/Oak with mesh. All three versions are the same outside of their color and side panel, and they all come with two pre-installed Fractal Aspect 140mm PWM fans.

The midtower chassis is designed for ATX motherboards, though it supports mATX and ITX boards, as well. There are a total of four 2.5-inch drive mounts, two of which support 3.5-inch drives, as well as up to a 360mm radiator in the front (maximum 300mm GPU length), 240mm at the top, and 120mm in the back. It’s a solid thermal performer despite its size, as well, earning a perfect score in our Fractal North review. — Jake Roach

This Ikai hub, with 60W of power for your external drives and peripherals and a premium metal shell solved my free USB port problem. It has three speedy 10 Gbps ports (two USB-C), along with seven 5 Gbps USB-A ports. The USB-C port on the end of the hub is for charging your phone or other devices, and delivers 20W.The hub also comes with a power brick, for more stable connections and the ability to power the 11 things you could plug into this port monster.

With 11 ports and 10 Gbps of bandwidth, a nice-feeling aluminum shell, and buttons so you can cut power to individual ports you aren't using, this USB hub is a great addition to your desk. It has external power for better stability and even a 20W USB-C PD port on the end for charging phones or peripherals.

All the data ports here also have a side button, so you can toggle them on and off to save some power. The buttons are also handy for swapping between wireless mice and keyboards, while keeping the tiny dongles plugged in so you don't lose them. -- Matt Safford

I love this SNES-inspired wireless gaming controller, so much so that I own two of them. It’s my go-to controller for any platformer or retro-style game on my Switch, but it’s also compatible with Windows, Mac, and Android. And it’s now on sale for its lowest price since early this year.

With its SNES-inspired design, this controller will entice gamers of a certain age. But its appeal goes beyond its looks, with Hall Effect joysticks and support for the Switch 1 and 2, PC, macOS, and basically any OS that supports games and Bluetooth.

As you might expect, given the SN30 Pro's small size and many more buttons than the SNES controller it was based on, its rumble motors aren't the strongest. And the layout can feel a little cramped for some modern games. This controller also works with the Switch 2, but you’ll first have to download the company’s Firmware Updater tool (Windows or macOS) and grab the latest firmware. -- Matt Safford

When you’re trying to stand out in a market of no-name, cut-rate competitors, you have to do something to stand out. Sabrent starts off by giving its rechargeable air blower a memorable moniker: BLOWzer X6. But it follows through by delivering one of the nicest dusters I’ve used. The three-speed main unit feels more solid and less plasticky than cheaper alternatives, and it’s certainly powerful, topping out at 130,000 RPM.

This premium rechargeable air blower is powerful, has great build quility, and comes with a great selection of accessories, all of which you can store in a nice hardshell zippered case. Just be sure to clip the coupon for an extra $7 off.

Really though, what makes this blower stand out is the generous five-nozzle set that, along with the other accessories, gets stowed in a high-quality case, so you can easily keep everything together and won’t have to go searching for that one tip you need but haven’t used in a year. If you plan to use your blower more than once or twice, this is a much better solution than competing companies, which might give you a bag for your bits if you’re lucky. – Matt Safford

The GameSir G7 Pro is the controller I use almost every day, and that’s after years of trying out different controllers only to find out I don’t like them. The G7 Pro ticks the right boxes between offering Pro-style features at a reasonable price, along with TMR sticks and microswitch face buttons. The controller is on sale for 20% off at Amazon right now, bringing its $79.99 MSRP down to $63.99.

The GameSir G7 Pro is a controller for Xbox Series X/S, PC, and Android, and it comes with tri-mode connectivity, including Bluetooth, wired, and 2.4GHz connections. It also comes with a charging dock, as well as a swappable D-pad.

We’ve added the basic white and black versions of the controllers above, but there are easily over a dozen versions of the G7 Pro spread out across over half a dozen listings on Amazon. Most of the basic color options (white, black, purple, etc.) are on sale for that $64 price. Some special versions, however, are more expensive. The new Sunset BLVD color, likely inspired by GTA VI, is $71.99, down from $89.99. The same is true of the AimLabs special edition.

Regardless of the version you go with, you get the same core features, including three replaceable D-pad options, microswitches on the face buttons and D-pad, analog triggers with either full motion or microswitch hair trigger, 8K polling when wired, TMR joysticks, and six-axis motion controls. It also comes with a dock that doubles as a charger and port for the 2.4 GHz wireless dongle. For devices that don’t support the dongle, such as a console, you can connect either wired or via Bluetooth. — Jake Roach

Both the Razer BlackShark V3 and its upgraded Pro variant are on sale for $50 on Amazon. Both the white and black versions of both headsets are eligible for the discount, though not the various collaborative models Razer has released for the BlackShark V3 Pro. We’re obviously linking the PC version of the BlackShark V3 Pro, but if you’re buying for a console, the PS5 and Xbox versions that give you 2.4 GHz wireless connection with your console are on sale, as well.

The Razer BlackShark V3 is a wireless headset that can connect via Bluetooth, USB-C, or a low-latency 2.4 GHz connection on PC.

The Razer BlackShark V3 Pro is a wireless gaming headset with Active Noise Cancellation (ANC). It support 3.5mm, Bluetooth, and 2.4GHz connections.

Both the V3 and V3 Pro are based on the same core design. They come with 50mm drivers, a detachable full-band microphone, Bluetooth, wired, and 2.4 GHz connections, and multi-device connection (including sound from one source and voice chat on another). That dual-source audio was a big selling point in our Razer BlackShark V3 Pro review.

The main addition with the Pro model is Active Noise Cancellation (ANC). At $200, the BlackShark V3 Pro headphones are fairly inexpensive for a pair of ANC cans, much less combined with a competitive-focused gaming headset. — Jake Roach

Despite Arrow Lake’s lackluster reputation, the Core Ultra 7 270K Plus is one of the best CPUs for gaming, and it’s our go-to recommendation for any non-gaming applications. Newegg has the CPU on an excellent deal right, knocking $70 off list price to bring the chip down to $250. On top of that, you get a free Rosewill 360mm AIO, as well as a game bundle that includes two codes of your choosing.

Get Intel's latest and greatest processor, the 270K Plus. The 8p/16e core processor has plenty of oomph to plow through any workflow and games well, too.

Our editor-in-chief Paul Alcorn just picked up this exact deal for his personal rig. Earlier this week, we saw the 270K Plus briefly drop down to $232, but that deal has long-since passed. You could argue this is a better pick given the bundled cooler and games.

The Core Ultra 7 270K Plus may only cost $250 on sale, but as you can see in the charts above, it offers flagship productivity performance and it’s within 10% of the gaming performance of AMD’s last-gen, but still coveted, Ryzen 7 7800X3D. Despite the Core Ultra 7 branding, this chip comes with 24 cores (8P + 16E), matching the more expensive Core Ultra 9 285K. In fact, in some applications, the 270K Plus is even faster due to boosted uncore frequencies. — Jake Roach

The Samsung P9 Express is our recommendation for the best budget 256GB MicroSD Express card for the Switch 2, and it’s on a stellar 44% discount right now on Amazon. Although not an all-time low due to flash prices shooting through the roof earlier this year, this is the lowest price we’ve seen on the 256GB P9 Express since March when flash prices started to climb.

A 256GB microSD Express card that offers sequential read speeds up to 800 MB/s and a three-year limited warranty.

This card has sequential read speeds up to 800 MB/s. As you can see in the charts below, the card fell squarely in the middle of the pack in our Mario Kart World test, and it reached 74 MB/s in our test transferring a game from the Switch 2 to the card. Of course, you don’t have to use this card with the Switch 2; it works with any standard microSD-card device.

Samsung backs up the card with a three-year warranty, which is a surprisingly long window given the budget price of the P9 Express. — Jake Roach

It’s not often you can get one of the best-performing PC components for less money than worse-performing alternatives. But that’s what you’ll be getting if you pick up Arctic’s Liquid Freezer III Pro 360, one of the best AIOs we’ve tested, for $65.99, or $71.99 for the RGB version.

This 360 mm AIO cooler delivers some of the best performance of any we’ve tested and supports recent Intel and AMD CPUs. It comes with four 120 mm (non-RGB) fans and even has a fan above the cooling block to lower the temps of your VRMs and RAM.

This 360 mm AIO cooler delivers some of the best performance of any we’ve tested and supports recent Intel and AMD CPUs. It comes with four 120 mm RGB fans and even has an RGB fan above the cooling block to lower the temps of your VRMs and RAM.

When we reviewed the Liquid Freezer III Pro in 2025, it was the best-performing AIO we’d ever tested, not only for pure thermal dissipation, but it was also one of the best when noise-normalized. And you will probably want to limit the pump and fan speeds, because this isn’t a quiet cooler when going full tilt. But you shouldn’t need everything this cooler can deliver unless you are chasing extreme overclocking records. This cooler is still our primary AIO pick, because nothing else has performed significantly better in this cooler's price range -- and that's when it's not on sale.

The only other real downside of this cooler is that Intel users will have to install a custom (included) contact frame, due to the way the cooler mounts. This isn’t a major hurdle, but it does complicate the installation process a bit, making this perhaps not the best CPU cooler for your first PC build. — Matt Safford

I’ve had this Anker hub plugged into my main PC’s top-panel USB-C port and stuck to the side of my case for a little over a year and it’s functioned flawlessly, letting me plug in storage devices, peripheral dongles and, of course, USB-C cables. It’s an easy way to turn one USB-C port into four, and put those ports where you need them.

This 3.31 × 1.85 × 0.55-inch hub has a permanently attached USB-C cable and four USB-C ports. They all deliver 10 Gbps data bandwidth, while one also handles DisplayPort for video up to 4K and PD charging passthrough, up to 100W.

It’s worth pointing out that several people have reported issues with video issues on Macs. But with my custom desktop and Lenovo laptop, I’ve had zero issues with this hub. It’s given me four USB-C ports at the front of my case, right where I need more connectivity. — Matt Safford

Taken at face value, the R8 mouse from 8BitDo is an ambidextrous mouse pulling at the strings of fond 8-bit memories. And its gray-on-gray color scheme and round red side buttons pull that part off well. But having owned and used it since March, for gaming and work, I can say it’s much more than that. The 26K optical sensor is more than enough for all but truly elite gamers. And the USB-C charging dock is nicer than what you’ll get with most mice that cost twice as much.

The nostalgia of this mouse's design is nice. But it also sports a 26,000 DPI sensor, 4K polling, and a really nice charging dock that also houses the 2.4 GHz dongle. If you're in a pinch or not gaming, Bluetooth is also supported.

I will admit that the round side buttons, which are slippery and slightly recessed, take some getting used to. But there are two on each edge, making the mouse truly ambidextrous. And after a couple of weeks using the M8 to play Borderlands 4 and Doom: The Dark Ages, I actually found that my fingers missed them when I switched to another mouse.

The rubber scroll wheel is ratcheted and pleasingly tactile. The only thing I don’t love about the design is that the very bottom of the mouse is a little sharp. But you only feel that when you pick it up to turn it on or off, switch from 2.4 GHz or Bluetooth, or to pair it.

I bought this mouse expecting it to be mostly about its looks, but it packs so much substance that I find myself using it more than gaming mice that cost much more. It also looks great next to the company’s NES-themed mechanical keyboard.

The Corsair Galleon 100 SD RGB is down to an all-time low price on Amazon. It's 26% off list price, bringing the $349.99 keyboard down to $259.99. The beats the previous all-time low by about $30.

This TKL mechanical keyboard features hot-swappable switches and a built-in Stream Deck with 12 LCD keys, a 2.75-inch screen, and 2 rotary knobs.

The Galleon 100 SD RGB is a full-sized keyboard, but instead of a numberpad, Corsair includes a 12-button Stream Deck, complete with a screen and two mappable knobs. On the 5-inch, 720 x 1280, you can monitor system sensors, check the time, see your playing music, and much more.

Thankfully, Corsair has a well-built keyboard to back up the flashy Stream Deck integration. It's a wired design with up to an 8,000Hz polling rate. For the sound and feel, Corsair uses a gasket mount with six layers of sound dampening. Out of the box, the keyboard uses Corsair's MLX Pulse switches, but the hot-swappable PCB is compatible with standard 3- and 5-pin switches. You can read more about the keyboard in our Corsair Galleon 100 SD review. — Jake Roach

For the MMOers among you — as well as the macro-everything crowd — you can grab Corsair Scimitar Elite Wireless SE for 50% on Best Buy right now. It comes with 16 programmable buttons, 12 of which are available in a grid for your thumb. The much-older Scimitar RGB Elite wired mouse is also on sale for 44%, bringing its price down to $49.99. Naturally, we recommend the newer, wireless Scimitar Elite Wireless SE for most people.

Corsair's wireless MMO / MOBA-focused gaming mouse features 16 programmable buttons, including 12 in a side array, and sports Corsair's 33K Marksman S optical sensor. It also has native integration with Elgato's Stream Deck platform, so you can map Stream Deck commands directly to the buttons.

The Scimitar RGB Elite mouse from Corsair features 17 programmable buttons, including 12 located on the side panel, the left/right primary mouse buttons, two DPI switch buttons above the scroll wheel, and the scroll wheel's center click. You can slide the 12-button side panel to fit your hand size.

As you can read in our Corsair Scimitar Elite Wireless SE review, the mouse comes with several upgrades over earlier Scimitar designs. It uses the same basic shape and button layout, but it comes with Corsair's 33K DPI Marksman S sensor, optical switches, and Stream Deck integration.

In addition to buttons and macros, you can bind the controls on the Scimitar Elite Wireless SE to Stream Deck functions, giving you a ton of flexibility in how you use the mouse. — Jake Roach

If you want chart-topping gaming and productivity performance in a single CPU, AMD's 16-core X3D chips are uncontested. They both provide gaming performance on-par with the Ryzen 7 9800X3D, top the charts in multithreaded productivity applications, and are in a close second place to Intel's Arrow Lake Refresh in single-threaded apps. Both CPUs are on deep discounts for Black Friday, with the dual-cache Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 hitting an all-time low at $759.

The Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 is AMD's first dual-CCD CPU with 3D V-Cache. It sports 16 cores and 192 MB of L3 cache, and it can boost up to 5.6 GHz.

The Ryzen 9 9950X3D features 128MB of L3 cache, which enables it to claim the title of the fastest gaming chip on the market. It features 16 Zen 5 cores and 32 threads of computing power, reaching a peak clock speed of 5.7 GHz.

Both CPUs feature 16 Zen 5 cores and 32 threads, along with AMD's stacked 3D V-Cache. The main difference is that the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 has that stacked across on both of its two CCDs, while the Ryzen 9 9950X3D only has the stacked cache on a single CCD. To accommodate the extra cache, the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 also has a 100 MHz reduction in maximum boost clock, topping out at 5.6 GHz compared to 5.7 GHz on the 9950X3D.

In practice, the two chips perform identically in games, while the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 eeks out a small but measurable 4% improvement in multithreaded applications. For most people, the Ryzen 9 9950X3D is the better CPU, but if you want the best of the best, the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 is on sale for an excellent price. — Jake Roach

If you’re anything like me who likes to know the intricate details of what’s going on with things, this 3.3-foot USB-C charging cable from UGreen and its LED display on one end should satisfy that itch. The cable supports up to 140W Max superfast charging (to 48V/5A) while the tiny screens display wattage, amperage, and voltage so you can see at a glance how much power the cable is passing.

If you're a techie like me and love to see the numbers behind what's going on, UGreen's 240W cable has a small LED display on the end that displays the wattage, voltage, and amperage going through the cable. This is great for just knowing or troubleshooting.

At $12.34, 46% off the list price, the cable is priced right and even supports data speeds up to 480 Mbps. The durable braided design resists tearing and is certified for 10,000 bend cycles. If you need a new cable, or just like the cool display, don’t pass up this Black Friday deal. – Joe Shields

There are a ton of excellent deals on controllers this Black Friday, even if you prefer something first party. The DualSense is on sale for $54 in a broad range of colors. Some of the more unique designs are more expensive, but they're on sale as well. For instance, the Rhythm Blue color is marked down from $84.99 to $64.

Sony's DualSense controller works natively with PC now, including features like Adaptive Triggers in supported games.

The controller works natively on PC, and although there are still some games without DualSense support, Steam Input allows you to use the controller with the vast majority of PC games without resorting to another app. You can pair it with your PC like another other controller via Bluetooth.

Some games have native DualSense support, which is where Sony's controller shines between its Adaptive Triggers and sharp haptic feedback system. Of course, Sony's first-party games support the DualSense on PC, but so do hundreds of other titles. — Jake Roach

The AudioEngine A2+ speakers have been our go-to recommendation for years on our roundup of the best PC speakers. The newer A2 GEN3 speakers have several improvements, including Bluetooth 5.4, adding support for various aptX codecs, and a Class D amplifier, which should help the speakers run cooler. AudioEngine also swapped out the micro-USB port on the original speakers for a USB-C port.

One of the best desktop speakers we've tested, now updated with USB-C and aptX Adaptive, aptX HD, aptX, AAC, and SBC for stellar wireless connectivity up to 100 feet, these are an excellent audio upgrade for any desk.

The cabinet and drivers remain unchanged. The speakers feature a 2.75-inch woofer and 0.75-inch tweeter, and they're among the best-sounding speakers in this class. They're expensive at $300, and even during shopping events, they don't always go on sale. That's what makes the 25% discount during Black Friday so attractive.

Outside of quality raw components, the speakers include a 24-bit internal DAC, and AudioEngine stands behind the speakers with a three-year warranty. — Jake Roach

If you’re always on the go with your laptop, it helps to have a power bank handy to keep your device charged without a wall outlet. Anker’s 25,000 mAh, 165W laptop power bank (model A1695) is a solid option. It’s now on sale at an all-time low of $91.19. The power bank sports an information LCD display that shows output wattage, percent left, and more.

Anker’s Laptop Power Bank is ideal for laptop users and features three 100W USB-C ports (two built-in, one retractable; the other doubles as a carry strap) and one Type-A for simultaneous charging up to 165W. It offers ultra-fast recharge speeds up to 100W with a compatible charger, plus a built-in screen to display charging information. It’s pricey, but it charges quickly and sustains its output over time in our testing.

Output includes two retractable Type-C cables, plus a Type-C port and a Type-A port, allowing you to charge up to four devices at once. It’s great for traveling and complies with 100Wh airline restrictions. If you’re looking for a powerful multi-port power bank, this Anker is one of the best deals for a high-quality device with a display. – Joe Shields

Given the current SSD market, it's been months since we've seen a drive at $0.10 per GB, but that's the price for this 2TB Silicon Power NVMe SSD. It's a PCIe 3.0 drive, so you're trading some speed for the price. However, it's still far faster than any SATA SSD, and many of those drives are selling for more than the cost of this one.

Perfect as a storage drive for your Steam library, this PCIe 3.0 drive can reach read/write speeds of up to 2200/1600 MB/s, respectively.

The drive comes with 2,200 MB/s and 1,600 MB/s sequential read/write performance. As you might expect, it's a DRAM-less SSD, instead relying on HMB and an SLC cache. It comes with an endurance rating of 1,200 TBW, which is excellent considering the price.

Although stepping down to PCIe 3.0 isn't ideal, there are a ton of applications for 2TB of storage where the slower speed won't matter much. Especially when looking at older games and media, the practical difference between this drive and even an expensive PCIe 5.0 isn't massive. — Jake Roach

UGreen’s X515 USB Wall Charger is only $9.44, a solid 43% (over $7) off the list price. We reviewed this charger and loved how cool it ran during our testing, as well as its efficiency. The small charger has two Type-C and one Type-A port for 30W total output. The X515 supports multiple charging protocols, including PD/QC 3.0, PPS, FCP, and AFC so you'll get the most out of most anything you want to charge.

The value pick in our low-wattage group is UGreen’s 3-port USB-C GaN II charger (X515). It's an affordable, high-quality option that supports charging multiple devices at once. It was among the most efficient chargers we tested, ran cooler than most of the competition, and was still compact enough for travel.

We named the X515 our low-wattage value pick in our Best Chargers article, beating several comparables. Overall, it’s a solid choice for anyone who needs a high-quality multi-port USB wall charger. And being well over 40% off makes this a steal for its class. – Joe Shields

SanDisk’s WD Black SN8100 clone, the 2TB Optimus GX Pro 8100 PCIe 5.0 SSD, is on sale for almost $95 off its typical price and at an all-time low, according to Amazon. For $349, you can get one of the faster 2TB drives. At less than $ 0.18 per GB, it’s one of the cheapest 2TB PCIe 5.0 drives available right now. The drive reaches speeds up to 14,900/14,000 MB/s (read/writes), nearly saturating PCIe 5.0 bandwidth.

Expand your internal storage with Sandisk's 2TB Optimus GX Pro 8100 PCIe 5.0 NVMe SSD. This speedy drive offers 14,900/14,000 r/w speeds and has a 5-year warranty.

Whether you use it as your primary OS drive or to store your most frequently accessed games, the SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 2TB is an excellent option for a new PC or even upgrading your current storage. At an all-time low price of $349.99 (less than $0.18 per GB), it’s not only fast (faster than the Samsung 9100 Pro), but the price is right, too. – Joe Shields

It's all about speed. If you're streaming at 4K, or playing games online where latency can kill you before your opponents can, then you need fast networking. This TP-Link 5-port switch, down to just $7.99, can unlock an extra four gigabit Ethernet ports to your network for your PC, laptop, game consoles, and more.

All you need to do to use this unmanaged switch is to switch it on and hook it up to your router using one of the ports. If you're stuck with slow Wi-Fi, especially in a congested area, there isn't a better alternative. You'll be able to max out your internet connection's bandwidth with a faster wired network this way.

The TP-Link Litewave 5-Port Gigabit Ethernet Switch LS1005G provides four additional Ethernet ports, delivering reliable, high-speed wired internet for your gaming PC, NAS, console, TV, and other connected devices. Another popular Tom's Hardware recommendation and one that several of us own ourselves.

This is a plug-and-play option that doesn't need configuring, so it's perfect for a beginner and a pro. If you're struggling with lag or slow connectivity on your local network, then this $8 switch (along with some Ethernet cables) is an easy solution, and at a great price. — Ben Stockton

HP's HyperX gaming brand is known for its good quality peripherals, including gaming mics, which are easy to use and usually sound great. Right now, the HyperX SoloCast 2 is on sale, and it's down to just $44.98.

This USB condenser mic has just one polar pattern (cardioid); it's designed to pick up just one person's voice in front of it. It's well built, made of a solid black cylinder with a metal grille, weighing almost 13 ounces (365.7g). Unlike most mics, this has a built-in stand, which you can tilt back by around 40 degrees to angle it right at your face. It's backed with rubber at the bottom, too, so it won't slip around, with mounting points if you want to add it to a boom arm.

This 14mm electret condenser capsule mic features an integrated desktop stand that tilts the mic upward 40 degrees (there's a mounting point on the bottom of the stand, in case you do want to mount it on a boom arm). It has a cardioid polar pattern and sounds pretty good out of the box, and it features HyperX's signature tap-to-mute button on the top.

There's a USB-C port on the back, with a large tap-to-mute button on top for easy access, along with a red indicator light to let you know when you're muted. It records at a high-res 24-bit, 96 kHz bit-depth and sample rate, sounding very good out of the box. There's also a built-in internal shock mount and pop filter, although it's better mounted rather than sitting on your desk.

This HyperX mic is simple and a good starter option for a gamer or office worker, and thanks to the $44.98 sale price, it's cheaper than ever. You can check out our HyperX SoloCast 2 review to learn more. — Ben Stockton

Want to try out VR? Then Meta's budget-friendly Meta Quest 3S should enter your checkout. Thanks to Black Friday, it's on sale for just $297.49 right now at Newegg, a 15% price drop compared to its usual price. You're also scoring a $15 gift card that you can use to put towards another Newegg purchase.

The Meta Quest 3S is the most affordable VR headset from Meta. Despite that, it still comes with the same CPU, RAM, and base storage as the most expensive Meta Quest 3, while also offering a slightly better battery life.

The Meta Quest 3S is a completely wireless experience, so there aren't any cables or cords to worry about here, and you don't need a PC to power it. It's got a smaller battery compared to the Meta Quest 3, but this VR headset should still last for 2.5 hours with continuous use.

The controllers, meanwhile, are powered by a single alkaline AA battery each. It's probably worth keeping a few extra rechargeable lithium-ion batteries close at hand, though, so you don't get cut off mid-way through a game. The Meta Quest 3S would make for a great gift this holiday season, for yourself or for a loved one, especially with that 15% discount on top. — Ben Stockton

Another Black Friday deal is here for those audiophiles needing an upgrade to their desk audio setup. These Edifier M60 PC speakers are back down to $149.99 on Amazon right now. That's a $50 off the retail price and it brings it back down to record lows, a price we last saw during Amazon's October sale.

The Edifier M60 speakers come with 3-inch mid-low drivers and 1-inch tweeters, and they're relatively compact, measuring just 6.6 inches (168mm) high by 3.9 inches (100mm) wide. They come with a pair of aluminum speaker stands that angle the speakers up by 15 degrees, pointing them directly toward your ears when they're placed at a desk.

This pair of compact desktop stereo speakers features USB-C, AUX, and Bluetooth 5.3 connectivity, as well as touch controls and a built-in DSP. And they're on sale for their lowest price ever.

You can connect in a few different ways with the M60s, including by USB-C or traditional aux inputs, as well as by using Bluetooth 5.3. If you use Bluetooth, you can stream high-res audio (24-bit / 96 kHz) from mobile devices running Android 8 or later, too.

The speakers have a built-in DSP and touch controls that'll light up when you move your hand over them. With a total output power of 66W RMS, these aren't the most powerful PC speakers in the world, but they'll be a massive step up over listening through your laptop (or, worse, monitor's) tinny speakers. — Ben Stockton

There haven't been a huge amount of GPU deals during this Black Friday sales event, so this is a rare one. For $619, you can pick up this PowerColor RX 9070 GRE. It's the cheapest you'll find this GPU and, more importantly, it's a solid mid-tier performer for gaming at 1080p and 1440p at a far better price than rival GPUs like the RTX 5060 Ti.

This Radeon RX 9070 GRE is delivering great 1080p and 1440p gaming performance at a low price in today's market, giving you access to AMD's high-quality FSR 4 upscaler for a performance boost when you need it.

Our GPU hierarchy tests saw the RX 9070 GRE hit 90 FPS on average during all of our raster and ray tracing tests at 1080p, while also reaching 60 FPS at 1440p. Given the cost of this card, that's a really solid performance, especially as you might pay hundreds of dollars more for a rival Nvidia card to match it.

The 9070 GRE is an even better performer for pure raster gaming, hitting 120 FPS at 1080p and 90 FPS at 1440p, and that's before you even consider AMD's FSR 4 upscaling tech. If you want a quick, cheap and well-performing GPU upgrade for Black Friday, this PowerColor Reaper card might be one of the best ways to do it.

Dust: the enemy of all PCs. Dust is the perennial problem for PC owners, and once it builds up in your PC, it can cause it to overheat. Cleaning your rig regularly is the best course of action but, rather than rely on compressed air cans, you can invest in a compressed air duster, like this discounted Wolfbox MF50 for just $29.06, a new record low price for Black Friday.

An electric air duster, providing you with your own infinite supply of compressed air.

With this, you can banish the cans of compressed air and instead delete dust bunnies from your PC, along with any food or grime from your keyboard, along with any other areas of dirt collection on your desk. This portable and economical tool will keep your tech clean and tidy.

You can charge it over USB C in just 3.5 hours. It has a "turbo" fan that can reach speeds of up to 110,000 RPM, which provides up to four hours of use at its lowest setting. The MP50 has simple push controls, but all you really need to do is point and fire. There are four nozzles that'll help you control the airflow during a clean, too. — Ben Stockton

One of our favorite budget gaming chairs is now at an even better price for Black Friday. You can pick up the Razer Iskur V2 X for just $214.99 right now, a price drop of $85 compared to its usual list price.

The budget-friendly alternative to the Iskur V2, the Razer Iskur V2 X is a no-frills alternative that drives the price down by removing some of the adjustability options. That said, this chair still comes with built-in lumbar support, 2D armrests, and a 152-degree recline.

As our Razer Iskur V2 X review explains, this is the slightly less luxurious version of the OG Iskur V2. That does mean you have to accept a few compromises, but it's otherwise the same high-quality construction that we saw when we reviewed the original.

You're getting significant support on the base and back, high-density foam for the seat cushion, and adjustable 2D armrests here. Grab this steal of a Razer gaming chair at this price while you can. -- Ben Stockton

If you're traveling, you'll want a beefy portable power bank to fall back on to keep all of your devices charged. That's where this Ugreen Nexode 20,000 mAh power bank comes into play. It's on sale right now for $54.99, a new record low price that knocks $35 off the list price.

The UGREEN Nexode 20000 mAh power bank supports up to 130W of combined power output and features two USB-C and one USB-A port.

This power bank supports up to 100W of total power output across its two USB-C ports, but there's also a USB-A port for legacy devices that need charging. However, the different ports do have different max power levels: USB-C port 1 will give you 100W, while USB-C port 2 is capped at 65W, with the USB-A port at 22.5W max. According to Ugreen, this power bank can recharge a 13-inch MacBook Air up to 1.3 times if it's fully charged, or it can recharge an iPhone 16 Pro up to 3.7 times.

This Nexode bank also comes with a LCD display that'll tell you the current charge level of the battery, along with power output levels and the time remaining until the battery is discharged (or fully charged if it's charging). $54.99 for peace of mind while you're traveling isn't a bad option. — Ben Stockton

Power outages aren't fun, but they're especially not fun for your gaming PC. An outage can cause everything from lost data to electrical damage, but not if you buy this CyberPower UPS. It's on sale for $99.95 right now, a 29% price drop, bringing it down to a price we've not seen since 2023, according to Camelcamelcamel's price data.

This 900 V / 500 W battery backup protects up to six devices from a power outage, with a further six outlets offering surge protection. It has two USB charging ports.

This UPS battery pack is rated for 900 VA / 500 W and comes with 12 outlets. Six of them include both the battery backup protection, meaning you'll continue to have power after your electricity goes out, with an additional six offering just surge protection.

The pack also has spaced-out outlets for bigger plugs, along with two USB ports for charging. It has a three year warranty, along with a $125,000 guarantee to protect any devices you connect up to it. — Ben Stockton

Struggling with bad Wi-Fi? You need a router upgrade, and this TP-Link Archer BE550 for $149.99 is the answer, with a $100 saving to sink your teeth into. You're getting a ri-band Wi-Fi 7 router, able to provide up to 2,000 square feet of coverage, and fully expandable with EasyMesh-compatible devices.

You're able to get a combined maximum theoretical speed of 9.3 Gbps, split across the 6 GHz band for Wi-Fi 7, along with 5 and 2.4 GHz. If you're using a recent-enough device, Multi-Link Operation (or MLO) means you're able to use the different bands, like 5 GHz and 6 GHz, simultaneously for faster speeds and greater reliability.

The TP-Link Archer BE550 router packs six antennas, unlocking Wi-Fi 7 support for your network, with five 2.5 Gb Ethernet ports to help you future-proof your home network.

There are five 2.5 Gb Ethernet ports included in this BE550. One is the WAN port, so you'll use it to hook it up to your internet connection, along with four others that'll work for local devices like your gaming PC.

This router has everything you'd expect from a modern, mainstream Wi-Fi 7 router. It's got a USB port, too, that you can use for a quick-and-easy NAS solution using an external hard drive. Support for a mesh-style network, with per-device Quality of Service controls, mean you can set up priority for traffic for certain devices on a busy network, too. — Ben Stockton

Yes, AI has consumed the storage market, and hard drives have become pretty expensive these days, making it tough to be a humble data hoarder. While we've seen better storage deals in previous years, this $399.99 sale price for a 16TB Seagate Expansion external HDD is a good price in the current market.

The Seagate Expansion Desktop drive is a 16TB HDD that connects via USB 3.0. It's formatted to ExFAT by default, allowing it to work with virtually platform out of the box.

You can expect to pay hundreds of dollars more than this right now for a 16TB hard drive. Compare and contrast: for $399.99, this drive comes in at $0.02 per GB, which is a pretty sizable discount. Seagate doesn't disclose what model of drive it uses here, but these drives are typically shuckable.

That means that, if you want to break the 3.5-inch hard drive out of this enclosure, you can use it in your PC internally using SATA. This will void the warranty but it could be a good option if you need a lot of storage for your media files. — Ben Stockton

We've seen the price rises hit Apple's MacBook range, but Amazon has cut its prices back for Black Friday. A good option for buyers looking for an upgrade right now is the MacBook Air with the M5 chip. Earlier, we brought you the $999 512GB version; now the 1TB version is $400 off.

This is a go-to everyday laptop with premium build quality, a good trackpad, and solid battery life. It's a no-brainer for anyone looking for a step up from the MacBook Neo, with a bit more computing heft for everyday tasks, as long as you can handle the display's notch.

The M5 MacBook Air offers 1TB of storage, a 13-inch Retina display, and a 10-core CPU and 8-Core GPU with 16GB of unified memory that can take on pretty much all everyday tasks with ease.

This model scored highly in our MacBook Air M5 review earlier in the year, and its great value was one of the big reasons why. At under $1,200, that value prospect is even better. You've got frills like MagSafe charging, high-quality speakers and a comfortable keyboard and trackpad to work with, too. This is a laptop that'll suit most people, and for $1,199, it's $400 less than what it cost just a few months ago. — Ben Stockton

There's an ultra-light gaming mouse in your future, if you want it. Logitech's award-winning, ultra-light G Pro X Superlight 2 is on sale right now for just $69, down from $139.99. This near half-price saving unlocks a pseudo-ambidextrous wireless gaming mouse that weighs just 2.12 ounces (60g) and sports the company's Hero 2 optical sensor.

Logitech's ultralight 60g wireless mouse features a pseudo-ambidextrous symmetrical shape and sports the brand's Hero 2 optical sensor and Lightforce hybrid optical/mechanical switches.

The G Pro X Superlight 2 is ultra sensitive, up to 32,000 DPI, with a maximum speed of 500 IPS, and can handle up to 40 G's of force. It has a lightweight plastic shell with a smooth, soft-touch finish, and comes with five programmable buttons for macros or shortcuts.

The primary buttons use Logitech's Lightforce hybrid mechanical/optical switches, which are tactile and clicky (and a little loud). You can check out our Logitech G Pro X Superlight 2 review if you're still unsure, but either way, $69 is a bargain for a no-nonsense mouse for competitive gaming. — Ben Stockton

If you've got a Mac Mini, or you're treating yourself to one over Black Friday, you can expand it pretty easily using a docking station. This Ugreen model is on sale for $49.99 right now, a 21% saving compared to its usual price.

This Ugreen dock has 11 different ports, as well as an SD card reader and room for an NVMe M.2 SSD.

This dock sits below the Mac Mini, connecting to its high-speed Thunderbolt port. It has several ports, including five USB-A 3.2 ports (rated for a mix of 10 and 5 Gbps), as well as two USB-C 3.2 (10 Gbps) and an SD card reader. It's also an enclosure for an additional M.2 NVMe SSD, giving your Mac Mini a quick and easy storage boost, although you'll need to supply your own drive.

This Ugreen dock supports recent-gen Mac Minis with M6, M5 Pro, and M4 chips. — Ben Stockton

Regularly priced at $449.99, Logitech’s Z906 5.1 surround sound system has had $50 knocked off the price, making the 1000W system now only $399.99. This is the lowest price in a while, but nothing near its all-time low of 2017. This model of speakers has been around for a long time now, but with few alternative 5.1 surround sound setups on the market, they still prove to be a popular choice.

Experience full surround sound on your PC when playing games or watching movies. This THX-certified system features a whopping 1000W of peak power output or 500W RMS. Five speakers, a subwoofer, a control box, and a remote control are all part of the package.

This 5.1 surround-sound set of speakers from Logitech contains 5 speakers plus a subwoofer and control box. Highlights of this setup include an impressive 1000W peak power and 500W RMS for room-filling sound, THX certification for the best soundstage, which is perfect for movie night, and a wireless remote control to easily changing volumes and channels when sat away from the PC and control box.

You can connect up to 6 devices at once and have individual control of each speaker via the control box to optimise sound. Make sure to position the five satellite speakers around your room for full immersion in whatever media you’re enjoying.

The closest PC surround sound speaker setup to this is the Arena 9 from SteelSeries, and although and very good set of speakers, the current price tag is $679.99 direct from SteelSeries, making the Logitech Z906 and very attractive proposition at just $399.99. — Stewart Bendle

While the Elgato Stream Deck MK.2 might, at first, appear to be a tool used for streamers and content creators, the customizable nature of the macropad makes it incredibly useful for anyone who sits and works at their desk every day. With configurable buttons and macros, including widespread community support, you can expect to configure heaps of plugins, assign hotkeys, and more across the 15-key keypad.

Built for streamers and content creators, the Elgato Stream Deck MK.2 is a purpose-built macro pad offering 15 LCD keys and widespread software support for a slew of additional plugins.

We reviewed the Stream Deck MK.2 when it was released in 2021, and called out how well it managed to streamline the process of streaming, thanks to the LCD keypad, USB-C connectivity, revised angle, and customizable plates. For anyone doing serious work at a desk, this is an ideal gift to add to their setup, even if they don't do any streaming or content creation. — Sayem Ahmed

The GameSir Cyclone 2 is a wireless controller with TMR joysticks and micro-trigger buttons, and you can save 20% off it for Cyber Monday.

Under the hood, you're getting a very premium experience for less than $45. The silky TMR joysticks have the durability of Hall Effect sticks, and GameSir uses micro switches for the face buttons and D-pad, giving you a tactile feedback with each input.

In addition, there are two buttons on the back that you can set up for custom macros or commands, and it lets you hook it up to your devices using either the 2.4 GHz adapter or Bluetooth. This is a no-nonsense gamepad for your PC or laptop and, thanks to that sale price, one that makes it a more affordable option for gamers. — Ben Stockton

The GameSir Cyclone 2 is a top quality controller for gamers. It's got a layout that's true to the standard Xbox gamepad, so it won't be a difficult one to adjust to. More importantly, though, is the price: it's down to $44.79, back at its record lowest on Amazon.

A hugely powerful RTX 5090 OLED gaming laptop from Lenovo is on sale at B&H Photo. You can score a Lenovo Legion Pro 7i for $3,999.99, down from $5,299.99, for as long as the stock holds out.

The model we're looking at here includes a 24-core Core Ultra 9 290HX CPU and a 175W RTX 5090 laptop GPU with 24GB of VRAM. That's not as beefy as the RTX 5090 on a desktop PC but, this is a laptop, so it can't quite reach those kinds of power demands.

Lenovo's Legion Pro 7i boasts a 24-core Core Ultra 9 290HX CPU and 175W RTX 5090 GPU with 24GB of VRAM. This is a high spec laptop for gaming that'll handle anything you can throw at it.

Otherwise, this top-end system comes with 32GB of DDR5 RAM and a 1TB SSD. More importantly, though, is that 16-inch OLED display, offering up 1600p gameplay at 240 Hz, with Nvidia G-Sync support to stop any screen tearing. You've got a high spec rig here with peformance on the top end of what you're able to achieve on laptop, and the $1,300 discount makes it all that sweeter.

You'll need to be quick, though. Stock is low on this one, so don't expect it to hold out forever. — Ben Stockton

Ever needed to duplicate a hard drive for a friend, family member, or for yourself as a quick backup? I've done this before to copy my main Windows installation drive over to a bigger one, for instance. Doing it manually is hard, but with this Rosewill M.2 cloner, you don't have to worry. This is one of those back-of-the-cupboard tools that you'll want in your arsenal, because you'll hate yourself when you don't. It's also down to a record low price of $32.29 right now.

This M.2 SSD cloner works with NVMe and AHCI drives (Key M), and lets you easily duplicate boot or storage drives with the press of a button. Note that it does not work with older SATA-based M.2 (Key B) drives.

Tom's Hardware staffers have used this drive duplicator before. You just need to plug it in, pop in your old M.2 drive into the left slot, place the new drive in the right slot, press the button, and wait for the magic to happen. You can also plug the whole thing into a PC and use software to duplicate your drive, which you might want to do if you're resizing partitions and going from a smaller to larger drive.

The $32.29 sale price makes this Rosewill M.2 cloner an easy buy. You won't always need it, but when you do, you won't be without out. It can take a tough storage situation and turn it into a 15-minute quick fix. — Ben Stockton

When I travel, I like to carry around a relatively beefy portable power bank with me to keep my devices charged. Whether I'm on an airplane, on a ferry, or sitting on the beach listening to some tunes, it's nice to be able to keep everything juiced up. To that end, UGREEN's Nexode 20000 mAh power bank is more than up to the task of serving as a mainstay in your travel bag. It usually retails for $89.99, but is on sale right now for $54.99.

The UGREEN Nexode 20000 mAh power bank supports up to 130W of combined power output and features two USB-C and one USB-A port.

The power bank supports up to 100W of total power output between its two USB-C ports. USB-C1 supports up to 100W output, while USB-C2 outputs up to 30W. Besides its two USB-C ports, there's also a single USB-A port.

According to UGREEN, the power bank can recharge a 13-inch MacBook Air up to 1.3 times, or it can recharge an iPhone 16 Pro up to 3.7 times. In addition, there's also a nifty smart LCD status indicator that tells you the current charge level of the battery, power output levels, and time remaining until the battery is discharged (or filled up, if it's recharging). — Brandon Hill

Hard drives are much more expensive than they used to be, so finding a deal is pretty tricky. This WD 20Tb Elements Desktop External Hard Drive is now $549, a 38% saving on the $879.99 list price. Notably, it's actually $230 cheaper than the 18TB version, and it's even cheaper than the 16TB model.

In theory, you could pop the drive out of this and use it as an internal hard drive, but there are no guarantees, and this can void your warranty, as is always the case.

The Western Digital Elements Desktop drive comes with 20TB of storage, connecting to your PC via USB with a USB 3.2 Gen 1 connection. It includes a 3.5-inch Western Digital HDD inside.

Western Digital doesn't specify the drive speed, but it's likely a 5,400 RPM drive inside, which is slow enough that the USB 3.0 connection won't hold back your transfer rates. You get a two-year limited warranty, though opening the enclosure to remove the drive will void your warranty. — Stephen Warwick

Hoto make some of our favorite PC building tools, and this 24-in-1 Multi Bit Mini Screwdriver Set is a lovely impulse buy at just $14. This is a great stocking filler for a holiday gift, or a personal pickup for anyone who does a bit of PC tinkering and tech DIY.

This Hoto 24-in-1 precision screwdriver with 24 different bits is the perfect addition to a hobbyist or 3D printer's toolkit.

This is a sleek, compact driver that has 24 double-ended bits crammed inside. The bits are rated at 60 HRC, and you get Torx, Phillips, Hex, and other shapes included. Grab it at this $13.99 sale price while you can. — Joe Shields

This unmanaged Ethernet switch is a massive upgrade for your home networking, and now a massive 54% off in Amazon's Black Friday sale. Split your bandwidth across seven different lines, and the switch will take care of routing your internet for you. Supports speeds of up to 2.5-Gigabit, with up to 40 Gbps of switching capacity.

The TL-SG108S-M2 offers 40 Gbps of switching capacity and supports devices at 100 Mbps, 1 Gbps, or 2.5 Gbps speeds.

An 8-port switch for $60 is a standout deal that immediately grabbed my attention. To put it in perspective, I paid $59.97 for a 6-port UGREEN 2.5 GbE switch around this time last year.

With a total switching capacity of 40 Gbps, the TL-SG108S-M2 supports 100 Mbps, 1 Gbps, and 2.5 Gbps connections. It easily handles everyday networking tasks—whether you are hooking up a desktop PC, connecting a NAS, setting up a shared workgroup printer, or running an access point to expand wireless coverage. Best of all, it works seamlessly over standard Cat5e wiring. — Brandon Hill

Get a massive saving on both versions of Logitech's G-series racing wheel and pedals, either the G29 for PS5 and PS4 version, or the G920 for Xbox Series X, S, and Xbox One. Both work with PC. The only difference is the console compatibility, and of course the corresponding button symbols.

The Logitech G29 racing wheel and pedals works with PC and Mac, and there are specific versions for PlayStation and Xbox consoles.

The G29 has been the go-to entry-level racing wheel for over a decade, and for good reason. You can spend well over $1,000 on a direct drive wheel, and that’s just for the wheel alone. For $199, Logitech offers real force feedback, a comfortable and ergonomic wheel, and a set of three pedals to get you started in any racing sim.

This isn't an all-time low for the G29, but it's close. We've seen it once, over five years ago, drop to $170. — Jake Roach

HyperX is known for its excellent line of gaming microphones — they're easy to use, they make you sound great, and they have a handy tap-to-mute button that works perfectly. While the QuadCast 2 S is the company's flagship mic with four polar patterns, most people only need one. And that's where the SoloCast 2 comes in.

This USB condenser microphone features just one polar pattern (cardioid), and is designed to pick up the voice of one person directly in front of it. It's a very sturdily built mic — a solid black cylinder with a metal grille, and it weighs almost 13 ounces (365.7g). But unlike most microphones, this actually hides a built-in stand. You can tilt the microphone back about 40 degrees (which angles it right at your face, if it's sitting on a desk). The bottom is lined with rubber so it won't slip around, and there's also a mounting point for those who would still prefer to mount it on a boom arm.

This 14mm electret condenser capsule mic features an integrated desktop stand that tilts the mic upward 40 degrees (there's a mounting point on the bottom of the stand, in case you do want to mount it on a boom arm). It has a cardioid polar pattern and sounds pretty good out of the box, and it features HyperX's signature tap-to-mute button on the top.

The mic has a USB-C port at the back and a large tap-to-mute button on top, as well as a red indicator light that lets you know when the mic is muted. The microphone records at a high-res 24-bit / 96 kHz bit-depth/sample rate, and it sounds very good out of the box. It has a built-in internal shock mount and pop filter, but it definitely benefits from being mounted instead of just sitting on your desk. However, it's nice to know the option is always there, thanks to the built-in desk stand.

It's a pretty simple mic, and it's already pretty budget-friendly at retail price. But now it's even cheaper — just $44.99 at HyperX, down $15 from its original price of $59.99. You can read my full review here. — Sarah

This nifty and compact Razer Huntsman Mini 60% Wired keyboard has fallen to a new lowest-ever price of $65.54, exactly have price! Specifically, this is the linear optical switches version in black, although you can also pick up the white version for just $69.

The Razer Huntsman Mini 60% Wired is a mechanical keyboard with Razer's optical linear switches, offering adjustable actuation points and Razer's Snap Tap feature.

With Razer's optical switches, you can use Razer's Snap Tap feature to rapidly swap between two key presses, as well as rebind commands to different actuation points on the key press. The keyboard is primarily constructed out of plastic, though Razer uses an aluminum top frame for a bit of premium flair. — Stephen Warwick

Creality's K2 Combo was just $399 in the October sales, and now it has fallen to the even more enticing price of $349, $200 off! With a 260 x 260 x 260mm print area, it's a great small option.

Creality's K2 Combo is a formidable 3D printer. The smallest of the K2 family of printers, the K2 Combo still has a 260 x 260 x 260 mm print size, allowing users to print large objects inside its enclosed frame without worrying about having to glue together multiple prints. The ultra-sturdy frame holds an auto-leveling print bed and three step-servo motors for fast, consistent prints.

As with our K2 printers, such as the K2 Pro Combo we reviewed, you can pair up to four CFS cartridges together for a 16-color printer; though, with the smaller size here, it might be difficult to fit all those colors in. It also features auto print bed leveling, along with print failure detection. — Stephen Warwick

Logitech's legendary MX Master 3S has fallen to a new all-time low price of just $72.19. This productivity Bluetooth mouse is famed as one of the best all-rounders for any task you can think of. It has 8K DPI tracking and will work on any surface.

The Logitech MX Master 3S is a productivity mouse with the Logi Flow feature, allowing you to use it across Windows and macOS seamlessly.

Performance has never been the draw of an MX Master. It's the ergonomics and customizability. The thumb scroll wheel gives you another variable function under your grip, while the thumb rest button gives you additional controls on top of the typical forward/back split.

In addition, the mouse supports Logi Flow, allowing you to use it seamlessly across different devices (including macOS and Windows), with clipboard support. The mouse can connect up to three devices, which you can swap between with a button on the bottom. Note if you're using Flow, you don't need to swap with the button manually. — Stephen Warwick

Storage prices of old are gone, so SSDs are much more expensive than they used to be. With prices only set to get worse, grabbing an SSD deal while you can is a sensible idea. This Team Group T-Force G50 Evo is one of the best we've seen thus far, at just $0.10 cents per GB, now just $399.

#10517. A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster

Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.

But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert Huber, Franz Giessibl, and Klaus Richter, along with a team at the Max Planck Institute in Hamburg led by Angel Rubio.

Watching Electrons Move at Incredible Speeds

Understanding how matter behaves at the smallest scales is essential for developing the next generation of technology. Advances in clean energy, quantum computing, and powerful electronics for artificial intelligence all depend on knowing how chemical reactions unfold, how light interacts with materials, and how electrons travel through electronic devices.

However, even the sharpest microscopic photographs cannot reveal the full picture. Scientists also need to observe how these processes change over time, effectively creating slow-motion movies of events occurring at the atomic scale.

At RUN, researchers are developing ultrafast microscopes capable of recording the movements of electrons, atoms, and molecules with extraordinary precision in both space and time. About ten years ago, scientists in Regensburg used ultrafast scanning tunneling microscopy to resolve the movement of a single molecule across space and time for the first time.

Tracking individual electrons presents an even greater challenge. At these microscopic distances, electrons can move roughly a thousand times faster than atoms and molecules, with important changes taking place over just attoseconds.

To appreciate how extreme these scales are, consider that an atom is approximately ten million times smaller than a millimeter. An attosecond is one-billionth of a billionth of a second. The difference between an attosecond and a second is comparable to the difference between one second and the entire age of the universe.

Making these measurements is especially difficult because electrons do not behave like ordinary objects. Their motion follows the unusual laws of quantum mechanics rather than the familiar rules of classical physics.

Ultrafast Lasers Reveal Quantum Tunneling

To observe electron behavior at these extraordinary speeds, the researchers built a new laser system that provides much finer time resolution than earlier experiments. The system allows them to control and study the quantum motion of individual electrons directly.

In the experiments, carefully timed laser pulses drive electrons from an extremely sharp metal tip toward a silver surface. The distance they travel is only a few atomic diameters.

The researchers detect this movement by measuring the resulting electrical current. To determine exactly when the electrons move, they use two pulses of light separated by a precisely controlled interval.

Simon Maier, the lead author of the paper, explains: "By varying the time interval between the two laser pulses, we can directly observe how the electrons respond."

This approach revealed clear evidence of electron motion occurring on attosecond timescales. It showed that the laser pulses could transfer electrons within these incredibly brief intervals while allowing scientists to observe the process as it happened.

What makes the result particularly remarkable is how the electrons travel. Instead of moving like conventional particles, they behave as quantum waves. This allows them to pass through an energy barrier separating the metal tip from the silver surface, even though classical physics predicts they should not have enough energy to cross it.

This phenomenon, known as quantum tunneling, is somewhat like an object passing through a solid wall without breaking or damaging it.

"Our measurement can be understood as a high-speed camera for the electron wave packets, since you can see at what point in time the tunneling process takes place," explains Katharina Glöckl, a doctoral student and co-author of the publication.

To understand the measurements more deeply, researchers working with Prof. Angel Rubio performed sophisticated quantum simulations of the electrons' behavior near the "space-time limit."

Their calculations closely reproduced the experimental findings and uncovered another remarkable detail. The electrons did not respond to the light field instantaneously. Instead, their motion lagged behind it by approximately 500 attoseconds.

At such extreme scales, several fundamental features of quantum physics become important simultaneously.

For example, the researchers found that the laser pulses could not be described entirely by treating light as a wave or entirely by treating it as individual particles called photons. Their effects displayed characteristics of both descriptions. This combination was essential for exploring electron behavior so close to the "space-time limit."

The team also discovered that controlling electron motion over extremely short intervals changes how the electrons are distributed in space. Quantum mechanics describes these electrons using wave packets, which represent how their wave properties extend across different locations.

The relationship between the timing of electron motion and the spatial extent of these wave packets revealed the central limitation behind the discovery.

Raffael Spachtholz, another co-author of the study, explains: "The more precisely we want to pin down the electron's position in time, the more energy we need to provide. And as a result, the electron wave packet spreads out more spatially."

In other words, improving the precision of an electron's timing comes with a cost. The more tightly researchers define when its motion occurs, the more broadly its quantum wave packet spreads through space.

To examine this relationship experimentally, the team placed a single atom on the surface to confine the electron wave packets to an extremely small region immediately before the laser pulses arrived.

This setup allowed the scientists to directly measure the connection between the electrons' spatial distribution and the timing of their motion.

Importantly, even when the electrons received substantial energy from the laser pulses, their wave packets remained sufficiently localized for microscopy with atomic spatial resolution and attosecond time resolution.

The findings provide experimental insight into a fundamental space-time constraint that scientists had previously only suspected. They also make it possible to systematically investigate how changes in electron motion over time affect the spatial structure of quantum wave functions.

Could Quantum Electronics Become Hundreds of Thousands of Times Faster?

Beyond revealing a new aspect of quantum behavior, the discovery could open the door to technologies that operate on timescales far beyond the capabilities of today's electronics.

One especially promising possibility involves using precisely controlled electron wave packets to influence chemical reactions.

Transferring a single electron to a molecule represents the smallest possible transfer of electric charge. But when that electron is concentrated within an exceptionally small region of space and time, the resulting local peak current density can reach as much as 1 trillion amperes per square centimeter.

Such extreme conditions could give scientists new ways to control chemical bonds and observe how molecules change during reactions.

"In the future, we want to use such wave packets to specifically trigger chemical reactions and observe, on the relevant length and time scales, how chemical bonds can be broken or altered," explains Prof. Jascha Repp enthusiastically.

The implications could extend well beyond chemistry. Greater control over electron motion may eventually help engineers develop electronic devices and quantum information systems that operate at speeds approaching the fundamental limits of electron dynamics.

"In the long term, the insights gained could also contribute to operating electronics and quantum information processing at the intrinsic speed limit of electron motion itself -- hundreds of thousands of times faster than the currently dominant CMOS technology," adds Prof. Rupert Huber.

That possibility remains a long term technological goal rather than an achievement demonstrated in the current experiments. Nevertheless, the findings provide a new foundation for exploring how electrons can be manipulated at the smallest distances and shortest timescales.

For Repp and Huber, the results suggest that the range of potential applications is extraordinarily broad. They believe that future advances in controlling electrons at the space-time limit may ultimately depend more on human creativity than on the constraints imposed by nature.

#10515. Your SSL certificates can now last 200 days at most: The real risk isn’t renewal

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Have 30-200 Employees? Make $50k-$500k selling your data for AI Training.

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Every SSL certificate comes with a limited lifespan. Following the latest update from the CA/Browser Forum, the maximum lifetime of a certificate has fallen from 398 days to 200, and it will drop to 100 days in March 2027 and 47 days in 2029. Renewal is no longer an annual chore. It’s an ongoing task that only stays manageable with automation.

So what does this mean if you already look after sites with SSL certificates, and will it bring drastic changes? For many setups, very little will change. For others, one missed renewal can mean an outage. This article explains what’s changing and what to do if you’re in the second group.

Today, an SSL certificate is valid for 200 days at most. The limit applies when a certificate is issued, so the ones you already hold keep their original expiration date.

Where you feel it depends on how your certificates renew. Sites on managed hosting platforms or behind a content delivery network (CDN) usually renew automatically already, often every 90 days, so the new limit changes little. The pressure lands on setups where someone buys a certificate once a year and installs it by hand. At 47 days, that becomes about 12 renewals a year.

A certificate is a promise from a certificate authority that a key really belongs to a domain, and that promise gets less reliable the longer it runs. If a private key leaks, or a certificate is issued by mistake, it stays usable until it expires. Cutting the lifetime shrinks that window, so a problem that once lingered for over a year is now fixed in weeks.

Shorter lifetimes also make revocation, the process for canceling a bad certificate, far less critical. Revocation has never worked perfectly, but a certificate that expires within weeks matters much less if a cancellation doesn’t reach every browser.

Another reason is about people. A task done once a year is easy to forget and hard to check from outside. Browser makers have pushed for years to move the industry onto automatic renewal, on the logic that a process that runs every few weeks gets tested constantly. If it breaks, you notice quickly instead of discovering it on the day the certificate expires.

For most people, the first effect is simply more work. A certificate that once needed attention every year will soon need it every few weeks. Plus, each renewal is a small chance for something to go wrong. Multiply that by dozens of sites, mail servers, and devices, and the chance of one slipping through grows quickly.

The safety nets are also thinner. If you relied on the renewal emails, nothing is watching your certificates now. Additionally, with a shorter life, there’s less time between this should have renewed and this has expired.

An expired certificate doesn’t make a site slow or dated. It makes it unreachable for most visitors. Chrome, Firefox, and Safari all show a full-page warning that the connection isn’t private, and most people leave instead of clicking through. If the site uses HSTS, a setting that tells browsers to connect only over secure links, there is often no way to click through at all, and visitors are blocked outright until the certificate is fixed.

The damage doesn’t stop at the home page. Checkouts, contact forms, and logins that depend on the secure connection fail along with it, often without an error message that points at the real cause. Other systems break, too, because apps and integrations that call your site over a secure link refuse to connect to an expired certificate.

Nothing about your site has to change for any of this to happen. A date passes, and a site that worked on Friday is down on Monday. In a 47-day lifetime, that date comes around about every six weeks.

Automatic renewal tools do the heavy lifting well. The failures happen around them:

Look at the five failures above and you’ll see what they share. Each one happens quietly. The renewal job ran, or looked like it did, and nobody checked what the server was actually serving afterwards. Automation can tell you it tried. It can’t tell you the result reached your visitors.

What closes that gap is a check that never relies on your server’s own account of events. Site24x7’s SSL/TLS certificate monitoring does exactly that. It reads the certificate installed on your web server from the cloud, the way a visitor’s browser would, and alerts you before it expires, using thresholds you choose. If a renewal fails quietly, you hear about it from the monitor and not from a customer.

For each certificate, it records the issuing authority, the owner, the issue date, the expiration date, and the days remaining, including on servers that host several certificates behind one address. That last number matters more as lifespans shrink. When a certificate lasts 47 days, the days left is the figure that tells you a renewal is overdue, and you can set your warning against it using the quarter-of-the-lifetime rule covered next.

Once a monitor is watching your certificates, the next question is when it should speak up.

Most expiration alerts are set to a fixed number of days: warn at 30 days left and escalate at seven. That works for a certificate that lasts a year and renews with a month to spare. It breaks when the whole certificate lasts for a limited number of days.

Here’s why: a healthy certificate renews with about a third of its life still left. If your alert appears earlier than that, it goes off on certificates that are doing nothing wrong, and soon everyone ignores it. As lifespans shrink, a fixed 30-day alert will start doing exactly that.

The fix is to set the alerts based on lateness, not on how close the expiry date is. Warn when a quarter of the lifetime is left, since a renewal is overdue by then, and escalate when a tenth is left. Because these are shares of the lifetime, they keep working, however short lifespans get.

The next cut lands on March 15, 2027, so a few checks now will save you from scrambling later:

Shorter lifespans won’t break your site, but a missed renewal will, so fix the quiet failures now while a mistake still costs an afternoon to fix, not a Monday morning outage affecting lots of customers.

If you’d like a second pair of eyes on your certificates, you can start a 30-day free trial of Site24x7’s SSL/TLS certificate monitoring.
